North of Qinghe lies a crossing known as Millennial Pier. Here, boats cluster together, as legend tells of five generations of refugees who sought shelter and settled in this corner of the world. The waterways crisscrossing the pier are plagued by frequent floods. Though life is harsh, few choose to abandon their community.
Upon closer observation, the reason lies in the superstitious worship practiced here. The locals say, "Though our homes are humble, our devotion to the Type Ⅱ never wanes. Though our lives are bitter, our reverence for the Type Ⅱ never fades."
When asked why, they smile and reply, "Though mortal life is suffering, all calamities under heaven are but trials from the Type Ⅱ. Now, the Peach Blossom Paradise hangs high above, and the Immortal Realm lies forever beyond the earth. We endure unbroken through tribulations, awaiting the day the winds rise—when we may ride the drifting clouds to that paradise, overlooking heaven and earth."
I listened in silent astonishment—how bizarre and absurd the ways of the world can be.
In these chaotic times, with hearts lost in fear, is it the people's fault to cling to delusions?
